newsitem.title: BELGIUM: Belgian blue chips seen pushing higher.
newsitem.headline: Belgian blue chips seen pushing higher.

text.p: The Bel-20 leading share index set another record close on Tuesday, and with no shortage of cash around to invest in the market blue chips looked set to continue their march into new territory, dealers said.
The Bel-20 finished 12.51 points or 0.53 percent higher at 2,352.15 after touching a new intra-day high of 2,353.59, with 4.9 billion francs worth of shares traded.
"Interest rates are still at a very good low level - that's providing good support, and the market remains positive on the dollar, while the Dow Jones is showing it can go up," one dealer said.
By the time the Belgian market closed the Dow Jones had climbed 1.1 percent to 7,561.

Meanwhile the Belgian benchmark ten-year bond yield edged down slightly, benefitting shares, as the debt market rode out the latest worries over European Monetary Union and whether a single European currency would be launched on time.

Stocks to gain included chemicals, drugs and films group UCB which ended 1.7 percent higher at 100,800 francs after chief executive officer Georges Jacobs told shareholders that ordinary profits were expected to grow further in 1997 and prospects remained very favourable in all its three sectors.
Non-ferrous metals group Union Miniere jumped 3.04 percent to 3,385 francs, continuing its sharp rise which began on May 30 at 2,840 francs.

As well as gaining from news on Monday that Bulgaria's Privatisation Agency had accepted UM's offer to buy 56 percent of its MDK copper smelter, the stock continued to benefit from a stronger dollar, good zinc prices, company restructuring and hopes of a dividend next year, dealers said. Union Miniere has not paid a share dividend since the 1990 book year.
Stock market newcomer Real Software made a sparkling debut, ending the day indicated at 2,195 francs.
The issue price of the offer had been 1,500 francs.

Subject to a twice-a-day fixings, Real Software shares showed only indicative prices all day after the high demand triggered bourse limits on price movements - set at a maximum move of 30 percent for the first fixing and five percent for subsequent fixings.
The morning indicative fixing was made at 2,600 francs.
"The rise is not surprising as the offer was 12 times over subscribed and their growth prospects are very good," one dealer said.
